Alex: ran a couple nsys captures after the perf regression on staging. seeing a recurring stall wave when KV cache miss rate creeps above ~10% — queue time jumps 30–60ms per request.
Maya: can you drop the short nsys snippet and the exact batch/window config you used?
Alex: sure. continuous_batch_window=12, target_batch_size=8. capture: /s3/nsys/1870000123.qdrep
Alex: nsys timeline shows lots of tiny kernel launches interleaved with host-side queue stalls. snippet from the timeline:
Alex: ```
# kernel timeline (condensed)
GPU: aten::matmul (fp16) 0.8ms
GPU: aten::add 0.12ms
Host: kernel launch overhead 1.2ms
GPU: aten::matmul (fp16) 0.9ms
Host: queue wait 35ms
``` 
Dmitry: 35ms host wait screams launch-tail / NVTX ordering issue, but 1.2ms per kernel launch is high. is this across many small kernels (micro ops) because quantized path split a fused op?
Alex: yes, when kvcache misses we appear to rehydrate attention blocks which triggers more micro kernels. miss rate ~14% on that run.
Maya: that explains it. more kernels => more launches => launch scheduling overhead explodes. did you check kernel selection logs? maybe the runtime switched from fused matmul->fused attention to per-op fallback.
Alex: turned on kernel-selection verbose, found fallback to klein_matmul_v2 for some sequence lengths. runtime logged: "fallback: kernel not supported for quantized layout -> using generic path" a lot.
Rachel: maybe a heuristic in kernel selector that prefers lower-latency kernels for long sequences but mispredicts when kvcache miss causes many short windows. could be the scoring function weighting latency over launch amortization.
Dmitry: try forcing kernel affinity override (prefer fused attention) for one run. also try bumping continuous_batch_window down to 6 to see if batching compacts those micro kernels into fewer launches.
Alex: just ran the forced-affinity run. results: queue tail went from ~40ms -> ~9ms p95. throughput slight drop but latency improved. attach short perf-bot analysis.
perf-bot: auto-analysis: nsys summary for forced-affinity run:\n - total kernels: 38 -> 16\n - avg host launch overhead per kernel: 1.1ms\n - cumulative host launch time: 41.8ms -> 17.6ms\n - observed kvcache miss-rate drop correlation: unclear (miss-rate consistent)
perf-bot: note: kernel fusion reduced kernel count by ~2.3x which reduced scheduling overhead. suggest adding a penalty term in selector that accounts for host-launch-cost * kernel_count_est.
Maya: nice. that points to selector scoring bug. likely we don't account for dynamic KV-induced op expansion.
Alex: agree. next steps: (1) instrument selector to estimate kernel_count given kvcache state; (2) add simple fallback: if estimated_kernel_count > threshold then prefer fused kernels; (3) run canary with continuous_window=6 and affinity override to validate.
Rachel: I'll file a short RFC and coordinate with runtime team. small perf test matrix: {window: [6,8,12], affinity: [auto, force-fused]} and record p50/p95/throughput + kernel_count.
Dmitry: +1. also add an nsys tail-run capturing host stacks when large queue waits happen (gdb-like host stack dump) so we know if it's scheduler spin or blocker.
Alex: thanks all. I'll push the canary configs and upload fresh qdrep traces to the ticket.
Maya: :thumbsup: keep the perf-bot summaries attached to the ticket so SRE can correlate with infra noise.
Rachel: tagging infra and runtime owners on the RFC later. :eyes:
